replies.rawMarkdown:
Even with the clarification, there are still plenty of questions.

I also do not want a situation where you publish your notebook at the start of the day and it ends up getting a higher score than my notebook.

The most charitable interpretation of the rules is that the leaderboard is determined based on the result display time, not the submission time. Under that interpretation, winners can publish their notebook in the final 30 minutes of the UTC day without getting “sniped.” It seems that notebooks on the top of the leaderboard need at least half an hour to score well, so by the end of the UTC day, even if many participants could clone and publish your notebook, they would not be able to get a public leaderboard score before the day ends. But this might not be the official interpretation.

firstMessage.content:
@gregkamradt

I'd like to check what the exact timing around the milestone prize is going to be. Note that as soon as we open source our notebook, we'll drop several hundred places because thousands of copies will be submitted to the leader board, and there is quite some variance. So we actually have a small window in which to open source. What's the exact time the milestone ranking is determined?

A note: other competitions such as AIMO had one point in time at which the milestone ranking would be frozen, then a separate deadline a few days later to actually open source and claim the prize. This means people don't have to guess their ranking ahead of time to make the decision whether to open source.
